928	    @staticmethod
929	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
930	        grid: GridMap,
931	        robots: Sequence[Robot],
932	        positions: Sequence[Position],
933	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
934	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
935	
936	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
937	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
938	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
939	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
940	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
941	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
942	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
943	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
944	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
945	
946	        *positions* holds the already-normalized tuple starting positions from
947	        :meth:`_normalize_start_positions`, paired one-to-one with *robots*:
948	        every route is walked from the tuple form so a first waypoint equal to
949	        the start cell is recognized regardless of how the caller spelled
950	        either container.
951	
952	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
953	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
954	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
955	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
956	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
957	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
958	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
959	
960	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
961	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
962	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
963	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
964	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
965	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
966	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
967	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
968	        """
969	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
970	        for robot, position in zip(robots, positions):
971	            route = robot.route
972	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
973	                raise ValueError(
974	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
975	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
976	                )
977	            normalized.append(
978	                _validate_route_walk(
979	                    grid,
980	                    position,
981	                    route,
982	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
983	                    checkpoint=False,
984	                )
985	            )
986	        return normalized

992	    def modify_obstacles(
993	        self,
994	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
995	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
996	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
997	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
998	
999	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
1000	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
1001	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
1002	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
1003	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
1004	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
1005	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
1006	
1007	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
1008	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
1009	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
1010	        distance is accumulated.
1011	        """
1012	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
1013	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
1014	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
1015	        if conflict:
1016	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
1017	            raise ValueError(
1018	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
1019	            )
1020	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
1021	        for cell in add_cells:
1022	            if cell in occupied:
1023	                raise ValueError(
1024	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
1025	                )
1026	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
1027	
1028	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
1029	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
1030	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
1031	        seen: set[Position] = set()
1032	        ordered: list[Position] = []
1033	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
1034	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
1035	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
1036	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
1037	            if position in seen:
1038	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
1039	                continue
1040	            seen.add(position)
1041	            ordered.append(position)
1042	        return ordered
1043	
1044	    def _apply_map_change(
1045	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
1046	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
1047	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
1048	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
1049	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
1050	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
1051	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
1052	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
1053	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
1054	
1055	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
1056	        # known to change the map.
1057	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
1058	        self._map_sequence += 1
1059	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
1060	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
1061	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
1062	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
1063	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
1064	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
1065	
1066	    def _map_change_record(
1067	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
1068	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
1069	        return {
1070	            "type": "map_change",
1071	            "tick": self.tick,
1072	            "sequence": sequence,
1073	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1074	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1075	        }

1077	    def _plan_route(
1078	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
1079	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
1080	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
1081	
1082	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
1083	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
1084	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
1085	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
1086	        """
1087	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
1088	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)

1090	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
1091	        for task in self.tasks.values():
1092	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
1093	                continue
1094	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
1095	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
1096	                continue
1097	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1098	            if route is None:
1099	                robot.route = []
1100	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
1101	            else:
1102	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
1103	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
1104	                robot.route = route
1105	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
1106	
1107	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
1108	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
1109	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
1110	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
1111	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
1112	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
1113	                continue
1114	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
1115	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
1116	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
1117	                continue
1118	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1119	            if route is None:
1120	                robot.route = []
1121	                continue
1122	            robot.route = route
1123	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
1124	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

1130	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
1131	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
1132	        cells: set[Position] = set()
1133	        for robot in self.robots.values():
1134	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
1135	                cells.update(robot.route)
1136	        return cells

1138	    def _safe_side_cells(
1139	        self,
1140	        robot: Robot,
1141	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
1142	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
1143	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
1144	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
1145	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
1146	
1147	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
1148	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
1149	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
1150	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
1151	
1152	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
1153	          skips anything else),
1154	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
1155	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
1156	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
1157	          route is excluded), and
1158	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
1159	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
1160	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
1161	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
1162	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
1163	
1164	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
1165	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
1166	        """
1167	        blocked = set(forbidden)
1168	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
1169	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
1170	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
1171	                continue
1172	            yield cell

1174	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
1175	        self,
1176	        blocker: Robot,
1177	        requester: Robot,
1178	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1179	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1180	    ) -> Position | None:
1181	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
1182	
1183	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
1184	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
1185	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
1186	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
1187	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
1188	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
1189	        """
1190	        return next(
1191	            self._safe_side_cells(
1192	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
1193	            ),
1194	            None,
1195	        )

1197	    def _self_sidestep(
1198	        self,
1199	        robot: Robot,
1200	        task: Task | None,
1201	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1202	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1203	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
1204	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
1205	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
1206	
1207	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
1208	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
1209	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
1210	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
1211	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
1212	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
1213	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
1214	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
1215	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
1216	        """
1217	        if task is None or task.completed:
1218	            return None
1219	        destination = robot.route[0]
1220	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1221	        if blocker_id is None:
1222	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1223	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
1224	        best_length = 0
1225	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
1226	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
1227	        # that order as the tie break.
1228	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
1229	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
1230	            if route is None:
1231	                continue
1232	            if (
1233	                blocker_id is not None
1234	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
1235	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
1236	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
1237	                )
1238	            ):
1239	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
1240	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
1241	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
1242	                continue
1243	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
1244	                best = (cell, route)
1245	                best_length = len(route)
1246	        return best
1247	
1248	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
1249	        self,
1250	        robot: Robot,
1251	        side: Position,
1252	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
1253	        blocker_id: str,
1254	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1255	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1256	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
1257	    ) -> bool:
1258	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
1259	
1260	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
1261	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
1262	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
1263	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
1264	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
1265	        never rejected here.
1266	        """
1267	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
1268	            return False
1269	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
1270	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
1271	            return False
1272	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
1273	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
1274	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
